chapter_theme: Concealment (மறைத்தல்), the fourth of the Lord's five acts: the Lord dwells in the heart and in everything he has become, yet the heart does not know his form; he shuts the soul into a body of bone and flesh within the bond of pasa, and even the three gods do not know how he did it. Like the eye that sees all but not itself, he is present and unseen.
structure_note: The Lord unknown though within (431), the soul enclosed in the body by pasa (432, 433), those who do and do not reach him (434, 435), his hiding in what he has made (436, 438), a turn toward grace (437, 439), and the images of clay and eye (440).

431.reading: The One in the heart, the light dwelling within, the One who never leaves the heart by a single step: though the heart and he are together, the heart does not know his form.
431.nuance: உள்ளம் opens every line, so the verse keeps returning to the heart that holds him and still cannot see him. That nearness itself is the concealment, which is why the verse opens this chapter. The variant line 3 (உள்ளமும் அவனும் உறவாயிருந்தும், though heart and he are kin) keeps the sense.

432.reading: The Lord who made birth for joy also shut it up in the sorrow of the bond that causes suffering; fastening skin and flesh to bone and binding it to what went before, it runs on to its end.
432.nuance: தோற்றசை is read as தோல் தசை (skin and flesh). முன்பிற் கொளுவி, fastening to what is before, is commonly taken as binding the body to past deeds; the verse does not say so. The point is that the same Lord who intends joy conceals the soul inside the body and its bonds. The variant அடைந்தனன் would say the Lord himself entered that sorrow.

433.reading: Though the Lord, Madhavan and the Vedic one who made pleasure, all three, come and gather together, they do not know how the Hidden One placed the great machine of a body that the Lord made.
433.nuance: மறையவன் plays on மறை, which means both the Veda and hiding: in line 1 it most naturally names Brahma, in line 4 it can name Siva as the Concealer. Which god the first இறையவன் is (Rudra, or Siva himself) is unclear. இரும்பொறி யாக்கை, the body as a great mechanism, is a striking image. The variant பரிசறியாரே makes the three gods the subject explicitly.

434.reading: Those who come to know, with a heart and a tongue given to food, the Lord who loves the light of the seeing eye, the First who stands as male, female and neuter forms, will not come near the workings of the distant pool.
434.nuance: சேண்படு பொய்கைச் செயல், the working of the far-off pool, is obscure. It may be the pool of births, which the knowers escape, or bathing at a distant sacred tank, which they no longer need. ஊண்படு நாவுடை நெஞ்சம் can also be read against the knowers, as the food-bound heart that cannot reach him; the syntax allows both.

435.reading: The first Lord, who makes the ways by which joy is given to the world that grows clear and to the gods, and the pure white flame with its coiled radiance, stands where darkness ends and yet becomes a dark chamber.
435.nuance: The paradox of the last line, beyond darkness yet a dark room, fits the chapter: the light is hidden from those he conceals it from. சுருளும் சுடர், the coiled flame, is traditionally taken as a yogic light, perhaps kundalini; the plain sense is simply a radiant fire.

436.reading: The one worth beholding, who made the limbs that yield grace, the sound, the desire that speaks, the many unlike forms spreading out and the earth, becomes these himself and hides in them.
436.nuance: அரைகின்று and கரகின்றவை are odd forms; கரக்கின்ற (hiding) is the likely sense of the second and carries the chapter's theme. அங்கங்கள் may be bodily limbs or the Vedangas. The verse is too compressed to fix beyond its drift: he hides by becoming his works.

437.reading: Knowing the kinship within, I hid the Lord inside me; coming forth, he grants grace again; and the greatness called joy and love, even when it comes out in open worship, becomes an offering too.
437.nuance: The verse turns concealment round: here the devotee hides the Lord within, and the Lord comes out in grace. வேட்சி may mean desire or sacrifice (from வேட்டல்), so the last line may say open worship is still an offering, or that it turns into longing. The verse leads toward the next chapter, on grace.

438.reading: Maheshvara, who fills all and stands as himself, Hara and Tirumal who go and move there, and Ayan on the flower who does the work: becoming these, he abides in harmony with them.
438.nuance: In Siddhanta, Maheshvara is traditionally the god of the concealing act, which may be why he is named first here. மன்றது செய்யும் (doing the work of the hall, or of the assembly) is unclear, and the variant கியங்கி யயந்திரு changes line 2. The verse makes the gods modes of the one Lord, as 386 and 404 do.

439.reading: Within the gathered bond, the excellent siddha sits on the great bank seeking joy; if one keeps to the rare bank of the Ganga in a way that does not reckon on the shore to come, impurity can be washed away.
439.nuance: A plain reading is bathing in the Ganga; a yogic reading, common in tradition, places the Ganga within the body and the bank at the crown. வருங்கரை ஓரா (not reckoning the coming shore) and the variant சித்தின் (of consciousness) for சித்தன் leave the subject unclear. அழுக்கு is likely the soul's impurity rather than bodily dirt.

440.reading: One clay becomes many good vessels; for all the wombs within, there is one; one eye sees many things but does not see itself; the Lord too stands in this way.
440.nuance: Two images close the chapter. The clay gives one source in many forms; the eye gives the seer who is not seen. The eye may stand for the Lord, unseen because he is the one who sees, or for the soul, which cannot see the Lord who is in it; both readings fit concealment.

links.note: 372 has Brahma and Vishnu, each claiming lordship, searching in vain for Hara's feet; 433 says the three gods together do not know how he placed the body. The gods' ignorance of Siva is the same theme, turned here to concealment.
386 gives the world-maker five sons and calls the creator the holy one; 438 names the gods (Maheshvara, Hara, Tirumal, Ayan) as forms the one Lord becomes and works through.

Both use clay and pot. In 1930 bindu stays in the worlds as clay stays in the pot, the material cause; in 440 one clay making many vessels is the one Lord behind all wombs, who like the eye is not seen.

431 says the heart and the One are together, yet the heart does not know his form (உள்ளம் அவனை உருவறி யாதே). 2101 says people set him above as one god without knowing him as mingled with them (விரவுஅறி யாமலே). Both name the same blindness: he is unknown not because he is far but because he is joined to the one who looks.

Both open with the Lord who made a birth for joy (இன்பப் பிறவி). 432 says he also shut it in the sorrow of the bond (துன்பஞ்செய் பாசத் துயருள் அடைத்தனன்); 281 grants that the toils of a sorrowful birth are many but says a birth mingled with him in love (அன்பிற் கலவிசெய்து) is where births end. 281 adds the condition under which 432's enclosure gives way.

433 calls the body that the Lord made a great machine (இரும்பொறி யாக்கை) whose making even the three gods do not understand. 467 lays out that machine piece by piece, the leaf-machine, the balance-machine, the forge-machine (பொறி in every line). 467 shows the contrivance that 433 says stays hidden.

434 names the First who stands as male, female and neuter forms (ஆண்பெண் அலியுருவாய் நின்ற ஆதி). 477 places that fashioning in the womb, where the forms male, female or neither (ஆண்பெண் அலியெனுங் கற்பனை) are brought about by the Light's power. 477 shows how the Lord's standing as all three forms in 434 is worked out in each birth.

435 says the pure white flame stands where darkness ends and yet becomes a dark chamber (இருளும் அறநின் றிருட்டறை யாமே), the Lord concealed. 1514 sets an old woman in the corner of a dark room (இருட்டறை மூலை) who removes the blind man's blindness and weds him, traditionally grace freeing the soul. Together they make the dark room both the place of concealment and the place where grace begins.

431 says the One stays in the heart while the heart cannot see him. 437 turns this round: the devotee, knowing the kinship within, hides the Lord inside himself (ஒளித்துவைத் தேனுள் ளுறவுணர்ந் தீசனை), and the Lord comes out in grace (வெளிப்பட்டு நின்றருள் செய்திடு). The chapter's concealment begins as the Lord's act and ends as the devotee's.

Near-repeat: 438 is 403 almost word for word (நின்றது தானாய் நிறைந்த மகேசுரன் ... மலர்மிசை மேலயன்), with ஆகி for ஆக. The same verse naming the gods as the one Lord's forms stands in the chapter on creation and again in the chapter on concealment.

439 says that keeping to the rare bank of the Ganga (கங்கை அருங்கரை பேணில்), without reckoning on the shore to come (வருங்கரை ஓரா), washes impurity away. 1498 says what the rare bank is: the shade of his feet (அருங்கரை யாவது அவ்வடி நீழல்), the one shore for souls coming toward it (வருங்கரை). 1498 turns 439's bathing bank into refuge at the Lord's feet.

Near-repeat: 2351 repeats 440 almost exactly, the one clay in many vessels and the eye that sees many things but not itself (கண்ணொன்று தான்பல காணுந் தனைக்காணா). The same verse closes the chapter on concealment and recurs in the chapter on the stainless states.

source_issues: 436: அரைகின்று and கரகின்றவை look corrupt (perhaps for அறைகின்று, கரக்கின்றவை); the verse cannot be read with confidence.
438: variant கியங்கி யயந்திரு for line 2 changes which gods are named.
439: variant சித்தின் for சித்தன் changes the subject of lines 1 and 2.
